metadata.title: Right-Angled Trigonometry in 2D/3D and True Bearings
metadata.vcaa_description: Use Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry to solve spatial problems involving right-angled triangles in 2 and 3 dimensions.
metadata.target_mastery: Solve multi-step navigation problems using three-figure true bearings ($000^\circ\text{T}$ to $360^\circ\text{T}$), back-bearings, angles of elevation and depression, and right-angled triangles in 3D space.

key_vocabulary.definition: A direction measured clockwise from True North ($000^\circ\text{T}$), written using three digits from $000^\circ\text{T}$ to $360^\circ\text{T}$ (e.g., due East is $090^\circ\text{T}$ and South-West is $225^\circ\text{T}$).

The true bearing from point $B$ back to point $A$, which differs from the forward bearing from $A$ to $B$ by exactly $180^\circ$ (add $180^\circ$ if $\theta < 180^\circ$; subtract $180^\circ$ if $\theta \ge 180^\circ$).

The acute angle measured upward (elevation) or downward (depression) from the horizontal line of sight to an object; by alternate interior angles between parallel horizontals, the angle of elevation from $A$ to $B$ equals the angle of depression from $B$ to $A$.

key_vocabulary.term: Angle between a line and a plane in 3D
key_vocabulary.definition: The acute angle formed between a slanted 3D line segment and its orthogonal projection (shadow) on the horizontal base plane.

theory.title: Three-Figure True Bearings and Back-Bearings
theory.explanation: In aviation, bushwalking, and marine navigation, directions are specified using three-figure true bearings measured clockwise from True North ($000^\circ\text{T}$). The four cardinal directions are North ($000^\circ\text{T}$ or $360^\circ\text{T}$), East ($090^\circ\text{T}$), South ($180^\circ\text{T}$), and West ($270^\circ\text{T}$). Because the North-South lines drawn through any two locations $A$ and $B$ are parallel, co-interior and alternate angles allow us to find the back-bearing from $B$ to $A$ by adding or subtracting $180^\circ$.
theory.callout_title: Always Draw a Compass Cross at the 'FROM' Point
theory.callout_rule: For 'the bearing of $B$ FROM $A$', draw a North-East-South-West cross at $A$ and sweep clockwise from North to the ray $AB$. Include leading zeros for angles under $100^\circ$ (e.g., $060^\circ\text{T}$).

theory.title: Navigation Components (East-West and North-South)
theory.explanation: When a vessel travels a distance $d$ on a true bearing $\theta$, its path forms the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle against the North-South and East-West axes. By finding the acute angle $\alpha$ against either the North-South line or East-West line, you can resolve the journey into a North/South component and an East/West component using $\sin\alpha$ and $\cos\alpha$. Multi-leg journeys are solved by summing the net East/West and North/South displacements.
theory.callout_rule: Sketch the compass diagram first, shade the right-angled triangle formed with the North-South axis, and label its acute interior angle before choosing $\sin$, $\cos$, or $\tan$.

theory.title: 3D Pythagoras and Right-Angled Trigonometry in Space
theory.explanation: To solve a 3D spatial problem (such as finding the space diagonal $AG$ of a cuboid of length $l$, width $w$, and height $h$, or the angle that a pyramid edge makes with its horizontal base), work in two 2D stages. First, apply Pythagoras' theorem or trigonometry in the horizontal base plane to find the floor diagonal $d_{\text{floor}} = \sqrt{l^2 + w^2}$. Second, use the vertical right-angled triangle containing $d_{\text{floor}}$ and the vertical height $h$ to find the 3D hypotenuse $D = \sqrt{l^2 + w^2 + h^2}$ and the angle of elevation $\theta$ satisfying $\tan\theta = \frac{h}{d_{\text{floor}}}$.
theory.callout_title: Draw Each 2D Triangle Flat on Your Page
theory.callout_rule: Right angles in 3D perspective drawings rarely look like $90^\circ$. Redraw the horizontal base triangle and the vertical elevation triangle separately as flat 2D right-angled triangles.

worked_examples.title: True Bearings, Back-Bearings, and Navigation Components
worked_examples.problem: A rescue yacht leaves Sorrento ($S$) and sails $24\text{ km}$ on a true bearing of $060^\circ\text{T}$ to a buoy ($B$). Find: (a) how far North and how far East the buoy $B$ is from Sorrento $S$ (give exact values), and (b) the true bearing of Sorrento $S$ from the buoy $B$ (the back-bearing).

steps.thinking: A bearing of $060^\circ\text{T}$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ clockwise from due North. In the right-angled triangle with the North axis, the North component is Adjacent ($24\cos 60^\circ$) and the East component is Opposite ($24\sin 60^\circ$).
Since the forward bearing from $S$ to $B$ is $060^\circ\text{T} < 180^\circ$, add $180^\circ$ to obtain the back-bearing from $B$ to $S$.

worked_examples.final_answer: (a) $12\text{ km}$ North and $12\sqrt{3}\text{ km}$ ($\approx 20.78\text{ km}$) East; (b) $240^\circ\text{T}$

now_you_try.problem: A hiker walks $10\text{ km}$ from camp $C$ on a true bearing of $150^\circ\text{T}$ to a lookout $L$. Find (a) how far South and how far East $L$ is from $C$, and (b) the true bearing of $C$ from $L$.

worked_examples.title: 3D Cuboid Space Diagonal and Angle with the Base Plane
worked_examples.problem: A rectangular shipping container $ABCDEFGH$ has a horizontal floor $ABCD$ of length $AB = 12\text{ m}$ and width $BC = 9\text{ m}$, and a vertical height of $CG = 8\text{ m}$ (with $G$ directly above $C$). Find: (a) the length of the floor diagonal $AC$, (b) the length of the 3D internal space diagonal $AG$, and (c) the angle of elevation $\theta = \angle GAC$ that the space diagonal $AG$ makes with the horizontal floor, correct to $2$ decimal places.

steps.thinking: In the horizontal rectangular floor $\triangle ABC$ (right-angled at $B$), use Pythagoras' theorem to find $AC$.
In the vertical right-angled triangle $\triangle ACG$ (right-angled at $C$), use $AC = 15\text{ m}$ and $CG = 8\text{ m}$ to find the 3D hypotenuse $AG$.
In $\triangle ACG$, use $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} = \frac{CG}{AC}$ to find $\theta = \angle GAC$.

now_you_try.problem: A rectangular room is $4\text{ m}$ long, $3\text{ m}$ wide, and $5\text{ m}$ high. Find (a) the floor diagonal $d_{\text{floor}}$, (b) the exact 3D space diagonal $D$, and (c) the exact angle of elevation $\theta$ of the space diagonal from the floor.
now_you_try.hint: Find $d_{\text{floor}} = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2}$ first, then compare $d_{\text{floor}}$ with the vertical height $5\text{ m}$.

worked_examples.title: 3D Surveying Problem — Vertical Tower Viewed from Two Bearings
worked_examples.problem: A vertical communications tower $OT$ of height $h = 60\text{ m}$ stands on flat horizontal ground with its base at $O$. Observer $A$ is due South of $O$ and measures the angle of elevation to the top $T$ as $45^\circ$. Observer $B$ is due East of $O$ and measures the angle of elevation to $T$ as $30^\circ$. Find: (a) the exact horizontal distances $OA$ and $OB$, and (b) the straight-line horizontal distance $AB$ between the two observers.

steps.thinking: In the vertical right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$, $\angle OAT = 45^\circ$ and $OT = 60\text{ m}$, so $OA = \frac{60}{\tan 45^\circ}$.
In the vertical right-angled triangle $\triangle OBT$, $\angle OBT = 30^\circ$ and $OT = 60\text{ m}$, so $OB = \frac{60}{\tan 30^\circ}$.
On the horizontal ground, $A$ is due South of $O$ and $B$ is due East of $O$, so $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$. Apply Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle AOB$.

now_you_try.problem: Using the distances $OA = 60\text{ m}$ (due South of $O$) and $OB = 60\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$ (due East of $O$) from the example above, find the true bearing of observer $B$ from observer $A$.
now_you_try.hint: At point $A$ (which is due South of $O$), the ray $AO$ points due North ($000^\circ\text{T}$). Find $\angle OAB$ in right-angled $\triangle AOB$.
now_you_try.working_summary: $\tan(\angle OAB) = \frac{OB}{OA} = \frac{60\sqrt{3}}{60} = \sqrt{3} \implies \angle OAB = 60^\circ$, so the true bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $060^\circ\text{T}$.

common_misconceptions.title: Measuring Bearings from the East/West Axis or Anticlockwise
common_misconceptions.misconception: Measuring a true bearing from the East axis (like standard unit-circle polar angles) or measuring anticlockwise from North.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: True bearings are ALWAYS measured clockwise from True North ($000^\circ\text{T}$). A direction $30^\circ$ West of North is $360^\circ - 30^\circ = 330^\circ\text{T}$, never $030^\circ\text{T}$.
common_misconceptions.counter_example: $030^\circ\text{T}$ points North-North-East, which is $60^\circ$ away from North-North-West ($330^\circ\text{T}$).

common_misconceptions.title: Placing the Angle of Depression Against the Vertical Cliff Instead of the Horizontal
common_misconceptions.misconception: Labelling the angle of depression $\theta$ between the line of sight and the vertical cliff wall or tower.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: Both angles of elevation and angles of depression are measured from a HORIZONTAL line of sight. If the angle of depression from a cliff top is $\theta$, the interior angle at the top of the vertical cliff triangle is the complement $90^\circ - \theta$ (while the alternate interior angle at the bottom horizontal is $\theta$).
common_misconceptions.incorrect_working: $$\text{Height } h, \text{ horizontal distance } d, \text{ depression } \theta: \quad \tan\theta = \frac{d}{h} \quad \text{(Incorrect — put } \theta \text{ against vertical)}$$
common_misconceptions.counter_example: Looking almost straight ahead ($\theta \approx 1^\circ$ depression) corresponds to a very shallow drop, not looking nearly straight down at the cliff base.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Find the three-figure back-bearing (the bearing of $A$ from $B$) when the true bearing of $B$ from $A$ is: (a) $047^\circ\text{T}$, and (b) $295^\circ\text{T}$.
step_by_step_solution: For (a), since $047^\circ < 180^\circ$, add $180^\circ$: $47^\circ + 180^\circ = 227^\circ\text{T}$.
For (b), since $295^\circ \ge 180^\circ$, subtract $180^\circ$: $295^\circ - 180^\circ = 115^\circ\text{T}$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: A bushwalker hikes $8\text{ km}$ due North from trailhead $O$ to point $A$, then turns and walks $8\sqrt{3}\text{ km}$ due East to point $B$. Find (a) the straight-line distance $OB$ and (b) the true bearing of $B$ from $O$.
step_by_step_solution: In right-angled $\triangle OAB$, $OB = \sqrt{8^2 + (8\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{64 + 192} = \sqrt{256} = 16\text{ km}$.
Find $\angle AOB$ from North: $\tan(\angle AOB) = \frac{8\sqrt{3}}{8} = \sqrt{3} \implies \angle AOB = 60^\circ$, so the true bearing is $060^\circ\text{T}$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: From the top of a vertical lighthouse $45\text{ m}$ above sea level, the angle of depression to a fishing boat is $30^\circ$. Find the exact horizontal distance from the base of the lighthouse to the boat.
step_by_step_solution: By alternate interior angles, the angle of elevation from the boat to the top of the lighthouse is also $30^\circ$.
Solve $\tan 30^\circ = \frac{45}{d} \implies d = \frac{45}{1/\sqrt{3}} = 45\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: A rectangular prism $ABCDEFGH$ has base length $AB = 8\text{ cm}$, base width $BC = 6\text{ cm}$, and vertical height $CG = 10\text{ cm}$. Find (a) the base diagonal $AC$, (b) the exact 3D space diagonal $AG$, and (c) the exact angle of elevation $\angle GAC$.
step_by_step_solution: In the base $\triangle ABC$, $AC = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ cm}$.
In vertical $\triangle ACG$, $AG = \sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ and $\tan(\angle GAC) = \frac{10}{10} = 1 \implies \angle GAC = 45^\circ$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: A light aircraft departs Mildura Airport and flies $120\text{ km}$ on a bearing of $300^\circ\text{T}$. How far North and how far West of Mildura Airport is the aircraft?
problem_solving_and_modelling.final_answer: $60\text{ km}$ North and $60\sqrt{3}\text{ km}$ ($\approx 103.92\text{ km}$) West
step_by_step_solution: A bearing of $300^\circ\text{T}$ is $360^\circ - 300^\circ = 60^\circ$ West of True North.
North component $= 120\cos 60^\circ = 120 \times \frac{1}{2} = 60\text{ km}$; West component $= 120\sin 60^\circ = 60\sqrt{3}\text{ km}$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: A surveyor stands on flat ground due South of a building and measures the angle of elevation to the roof as $30^\circ$. After walking $40\text{ m}$ due North directly towards the building, the angle of elevation to the roof is $60^\circ$. Find the exact vertical height $h$ of the building.
step_by_step_solution: Let $x$ be the horizontal distance from the second observation point to the building, so $h = x\tan 60^\circ = x\sqrt{3}$.
From the first point ($x + 40\text{ m}$ away), $\tan 30^\circ = \frac{h}{x + 40} \implies \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{x\sqrt{3}}{x + 40} \implies x + 40 = 3x \implies x = 20\text{ m}$.
Substitute $x = 20$ to obtain $h = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: A right square-based pyramid $ABCDV$ (modelling a glass skylight) has a horizontal square base $ABCD$ of side length $10\sqrt{2}\text{ m}$ and vertical apex height $OV = 10\text{ m}$ directly above the base centre $O$. Find (a) the distance $OA$ from the centre $O$ to a base corner $A$, (b) the sloping edge length $VA$, and (c) the angle of elevation $\angle VAO$ of a sloping edge from the base.
step_by_step_solution: The full diagonal of the square base is $AC = \sqrt{(10\sqrt{2})^2 + (10\sqrt{2})^2} = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ m}$, so $OA = \frac{1}{2}AC = 10\text{ m}$.

In vertical right-angled $\triangle AOV$, $VA = \sqrt{OA^2 + OV^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ m}$ and $\tan(\angle VAO) = \frac{OV}{OA} = \frac{10}{10} = 1 \implies \angle VAO = 45^\circ$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: Ship $P$ leaves port $O$ at $09{:}00$ and sails on a bearing of $030^\circ\text{T}$ at $12\text{ km/h}$. Ship $Q$ leaves the same port $O$ at $09{:}00$ and sails on a bearing of $120^\circ\text{T}$ at $16\text{ km/h}$. Find the straight-line distance between the two ships at $11{:}00$.
step_by_step_solution: After $2$ hours, Ship $P$ has travelled $OP = 2 \times 12 = 24\text{ km}$ and Ship $Q$ has travelled $OQ = 2 \times 16 = 32\text{ km}$.

The angle between bearings $030^\circ\text{T}$ and $120^\circ\text{T}$ is $120^\circ - 30^\circ = 90^\circ$, so $\triangle POQ$ is right-angled at $O$: $PQ = \sqrt{24^2 + 32^2} = \sqrt{1600} = 40\text{ km}$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: In a cube of side length $a$, let $\alpha$ be the angle that a face diagonal makes with an edge ($45^\circ$), and let $\beta$ be the angle that the 3D space diagonal makes with the horizontal base face. Prove that $\tan\beta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and hence explain why $\beta < 45^\circ$.
step_by_step_solution: The horizontal base diagonal of a cube of side $a$ has length $d_{\text{floor}} = \sqrt{a^2 + a^2} = a\sqrt{2}$, while the vertical height is $a$.
Therefore $\tan\beta = \frac{a}{a\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} < 1 = \tan 45^\circ$; because $\tan\theta$ is strictly increasing for $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$, $\beta < 45^\circ$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: Prove using co-interior and reflex angles that if the true bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $\theta$ (where $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$), then the true bearing of $A$ from $B$ is always $\theta + 180^\circ$.
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: The North rays at $A$ and $B$ are parallel; the co-interior angle to $\theta$ is $180^\circ - \theta$ (anticlockwise from North at $B$), so the clockwise bearing is $360^\circ - (180^\circ - \theta) = \theta + 180^\circ$
step_by_step_solution: Draw parallel North rays $N_A$ at $A$ and $N_B$ at $B$ cut by the transversal segment $AB$.

The co-interior angle between $N_B$ and $BA$ (measured anticlockwise from North at $B$) is $180^\circ - \theta$, so the clockwise angle from $N_B$ around to $BA$ is $360^\circ - (180^\circ - \theta) = \theta + 180^\circ$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: A vertical flagpole of height $h$ stands at the corner $C$ of a horizontal rectangular courtyard $ABCD$ of length $AB = 40\text{ m}$ and width $BC = 30\text{ m}$. If the angle of elevation of the top of the flagpole from the opposite corner $A$ is $30^\circ$, find the exact height $h$ of the flagpole.
step_by_step_solution: First find the horizontal diagonal distance across the courtyard: $AC = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = 50\text{ m}$.
In the vertical right-angled triangle at $C$, $h = AC\tan 30^\circ = 50 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ m}$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: A drone flies $300\text{ m}$ due East from take-off pad $O$, then $400\text{ m}$ due North, and simultaneously climbs vertically to an altitude of $500\text{ m}$ above the ground. Find (a) its horizontal ground distance from $O$, (b) its direct 3D straight-line distance from $O$, and (c) its angle of elevation from $O$.
step_by_step_solution: The horizontal ground displacement is $d_{\text{floor}} = \sqrt{300^2 + 400^2} = 500\text{ m}$.

With vertical altitude $h = 500\text{ m}$, the 3D distance is $D = \sqrt{500^2 + 500^2} = 500\sqrt{2}\text{ m}$ and the angle of elevation satisfies $\tan\theta = \frac{500}{500} = 1 \implies \theta = 45^\circ$.
